subtopic: Loop Invariant Code Motion safety conditions
learningObjective: State the safety conditions under which a loop-invariant computation can be hoisted out of a loop.
irSnippet:
; Original loop (SSA CFG)
; Loop header: bb_header
; Loop body: bb_body containing:
;   %inv = sdiv i32 %a, %b     ; loop-invariant in %a, %b
;   %use = add i32 %inv, %i
; Loop preheader: bb_preheader (dominates the loop; single predecessor of header)
; Loop backedge closes bb_body -> bb_header.
stem: The expression `%inv = sdiv i32 %a, %b` is loop-invariant. Under LICM, which conditions must hold for it to be safe to hoist `%inv` to the loop preheader?

options.text: (1) The instruction is loop-invariant (operands defined outside the loop or themselves loop-invariant). (2) It dominates every use inside the loop, or has no side effects when speculated. (3) Its execution is safe in the preheader (no fault, no observable side effect) — for `sdiv`, this typically means %b is provably non-zero, otherwise hoisting can introduce a divide-by-zero that never occurred in the original loop body.
The instruction just needs to be loop-invariant; hoisting is always safe because the value would have been computed inside the loop anyway.
Only pure instructions with side-effect-free operations (add, sub, mul) can be hoisted; divisions must remain in the loop regardless of invariance.
Hoisting requires unrolling the loop first to prove the operation executes at least once.

explanation: LICM safety requires: (1) loop-invariance; (2) dominance of exits so the hoisted value is used correctly; (3) speculative-safety — hoisting must not introduce faults or side effects that would not have occurred originally. For sdiv, the divisor must be provably non-zero (otherwise the original loop might never execute the body, e.g., a zero-trip loop, and hoisting would introduce a spurious trap). Options B, C, D are wrong: B ignores the speculative-safety condition; C over-restricts to arithmetic operations; D requires unnecessary transformations.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: all three conditions (invariance, dominance, speculative-safety) apply.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: overlooks that the loop might not execute; hoisting introduces new side effects if the loop body was never entered.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: divisions can be hoisted when non-zero divisor is proven; not category-blocked.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: unrolling is a separate transformation; LICM does not require it.

assumptions: Standard LICM as described in EAC3 and LLVM's implementation.
SSA-based analysis of loop structure with a well-defined preheader.
nonImplications: Does not imply LICM always helps performance; hoisting can increase register pressure and force spills.
Does not imply LICM only applies to arithmetic; loads with proven no-alias to intervening stores can also be hoisted.

distractorRationales.B: Ignores the speculative-safety condition (loop may not execute).
